planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; a ground-hugging evergreen species from the Russian Far East.

directions: This low, evergreen species hugs the ground with small, rounded, heart-shaped leaflets that deepen to maroon tones over winter and spreads outward each year on thin, far-traveling rhizomes, making it a useful slow groundcover under trees. Its showy lavender-pink flowers have broad, reflexed sepals that arch above the down-curving spurs like small wings, opening in spring above the previous year's foliage. Once rhizomes are established the plant tolerates dry shade better than many woodland perennials, needing only occasional watering through summer heat. Trim old, weathered leaves back in late winter just before new growth and flower stalks emerge.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; a bold, cold-hardy evergreen species from the Lu Shan region of Jiangxi Province, China.

directions: Described from the Lu Shan area of Jiangxi Province, China, this species carries unusually large, substantial evergreen leaflets that stand up well through harsh winters, among the toughest evergreen foliage in the genus. Flowers combine green inner sepals with bright yellow spurs, a two-tone effect that reads clearly even from a distance in a shaded border. New spring growth can show soft pastel coloring before settling to its mature green, and some selections pick up reddish tints again in fall. Because of its cold tolerance, it is a good choice for gardeners in colder zones who still want reliable evergreen winter structure from an epimedium.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall in humus-rich, moist, well-drained soil in full shade; a diminutive Japanese species.

directions: A small Japanese species sometimes debated among taxonomists as a stabilized form of the more widespread Young's epimedium rather than a fully distinct species, but distinct enough in cultivation to be grown and traded under its own name. Small, rounded leaflets about an inch across emerge bronze in spring before turning green with fine maroon flecking, staying compact all season. White flowers with small grandiflorum-like spurs appear on short stems just above the foliage, scaled down to match the plant's miniature stature. Its small size makes it best suited to a shaded rock garden, trough, or the front edge of a woodland bed where larger epimediums would overwhelm it.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; a naturally occurring Japanese hybrid of debated but long-recognized taxonomic standing.

directions: This semi-evergreen natural hybrid arose in Japan where the ranges of its parent species overlap, and shows traits of both in a tidy, clump-forming plant. Spring foliage is lime-green flecked with dark purple, and each leaflet carries a thin, dark maroon line tracing the leaf edge like a fine pen stroke; fall color shifts to taupe, scarlet, and red with contrasting green veins. Small, down-curving dark lavender flowers open on short stems in spring, followed later in the season by taller secondary foliage growth. Grow in reliably moist, humus-rich woodland soil and remove old leaves in late winter to showcase the spring bloom and fresh foliage color.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; a fertile natural hybrid found around Japan's Seto Inland Sea on Honshu and Kyushu.

directions: This naturally occurring, fertile hybrid between two Japanese species arose in the wild around the Seto Inland Sea and is itself variable enough that gardeners grow several distinct clonal selections under its name. Evergreen to semi-evergreen leaflets take on bronzed tones in spring and fall, and some selections have noticeably spined leaf margins that add texture to the woodland garden through winter. Sprays of small white flowers open in spring in step with the longspur epimedium's bloom time, held clear of the foliage on wiry stems. Plant in consistently moist, humus-rich soil in shade and clear away tattered old leaves in late winter before new growth begins.
